messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Religion and values, Social behaviour and attitudes, Political behaviour and attitudes, Government, political systems and organisations, SOCIAL STRATIFICATION AND GROUPINGS, Family life and marriage, and Economic systems and development in United Kingdom during the 1990s?
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: UK Data Service British Social Attitudes Survey 1990s dataset religion politics family
UK Data Service British Household Panel Survey 1991 2000 dataset
UK Data Service 1990s British Election Study 1992 1997 dataset
UK Data Service 1991 census samples of anonymised records dataset
action.query: UK Data Service British Social Attitudes Survey 1990s dataset religion politics family

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"British Household Panel Survey: Waves 1-18, 1991-2009","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.5255/UKDA-SN-5151-2","justification":"One of the most comprehensive longitudinal datasets for studying British society during the 1990s. The survey began in 1991 and follows individuals and households over time. It covers religious affiliation, social attitudes, political preferences, social class, employment, income, household composition, marriage, family relationships, and economic circumstances. The 1991-1999 waves are particularly relevant for examining changes in social stratification, family life, economic inequality, and political attitudes in the United Kingdom."},{"title":"British Elections, 1963-1992","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.5255/UKDA-SN-3175-1","justification":"A collection of British general election surveys covering political behaviour, voting preferences, party identification, political ideology, and attitudes toward government and political institutions. The 1992 election data are particularly useful for investigating political behaviour and attitudes at the beginning of the 1990s. The collection also supports historical comparisons with earlier elections."},{"title":"British Social Attitudes Survey, 1998","url_or_doi":"https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/4131","justification":"A nationally representative social attitudes survey providing information about British public opinion in 1998. Relevant subjects include social values, political attitudes, government policies, economic inequality, household income, social class, and demographic characteristics. It is particularly useful for examining relationships between socioeconomic position and social or political attitudes during the late 1990s."},{"title":"British Social Attitudes Survey Series","url_or_doi":"https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/3572","justification":"The British Social Attitudes surveys provide repeated observations of public attitudes toward religion, morality, family relationships, gender roles, welfare, government, political institutions, and socioeconomic inequality. The series includes surveys conducted throughout the 1990s, allowing researchers to examine changes in British values and social behaviour over the decade. Its repeated questions make it especially valuable for longitudinal comparisons of aggregate attitudes."},{"title":"Northern Ireland Social Attitudes Survey, 1989-1996","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.5255/UKDA-Series-2000041","justification":"A series of surveys examining changes in social attitudes in Northern Ireland between 1989 and 1996. It is especially relevant for studying social values, religion, political attitudes, national identity, and social divisions during the 1990s. The dataset provides an important Northern Ireland perspective that complements surveys covering Great Britain, making it valuable for research across the United Kingdom."},{"title":"Northern Ireland Life and Times Survey","url_or_doi":"https://www.ark.ac.uk/nilt/","justification":"A social survey series that began in 1998, providing information on public attitudes and social conditions in Northern Ireland. Relevant subjects include religious identity, community relations, political preferences, governance, social inequality, family life, and cultural values. The 1998 and 1999 surveys are particularly useful for analysing political and social attitudes surrounding the Good Friday Agreement and changes in Northern Ireland's political institutions."},{"title":"Census 1991: Individual Sample of Anonymised Records for Great Britain","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.57906/9c9n-9909","justification":"An individual-level dataset derived from the 1991 Census, suitable for analysing social stratification and population characteristics in Great Britain. It contains demographic and socioeconomic information useful for examining occupational class, employment, education, household characteristics, ethnicity, and regional inequalities. It provides a detailed baseline for studying British social and economic structures at the beginning of the 1990s."},{"title":"Census 1991: Household Sample of Anonymised Records for Great Britain","url_or_doi":"https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/7211","justification":"A 1% sample of households and their members from the 1991 Census in Great Britain. Particularly relevant for research on family life, marriage, household structure, social class, employment, and socioeconomic differences. The household-level structure allows researchers to investigate relationships between household composition, occupational status, and living arrangements during the early 1990s."},{"title":"British Candidate Study, 1992","url_or_doi":"https://pippa-norris-5b3x.squarespace.com/data","justification":"A survey of parliamentary candidates and members of Parliament associated with the 1992 British general election. It includes information about political attitudes, ideological preferences, social backgrounds, and political recruitment. Particularly relevant for studying political organisations, parliamentary representation, social stratification among political elites, and the relationship between social background and political behaviour."},{"title":"British Representation Study, 1997","url_or_doi":"https://pippa-norris-5b3x.squarespace.com/data","justification":"A survey of parliamentary candidates and MPs from major political parties during the 1997 British general election. It examines political values, attitudes, experience, and social background. The dataset is especially valuable for investigating political representation, recruitment into political organisations, social class and political participation, and differences between political parties during the transition from Conservative to Labour government."},{"title":"International Social Survey Programme: Religion II, 1998","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/issp/modules/issp-modules-by-topic/religion","justification":"An international comparative survey module focusing on religion and religious values, with Great Britain included among participating countries. It provides information about religious beliefs, religious participation, attitudes toward religious institutions, morality, and the influence of religion on social life. The 1998 wave is particularly useful for studying religious identities and values in Britain during the late 1990s and comparing them internationally."},{"title":"International Social Survey Programme: Family and Changing Gender Roles II, 1994","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/issp/modules/issp-modules-by-topic/family-and-changing-gender-roles","justification":"A comparative social survey module conducted in 1994 that examines attitudes toward marriage, family responsibilities, gender equality, employment, and domestic roles. The British data are particularly useful for studying changing family values, perceptions of women's employment, division of household responsibilities, and traditional versus modern gender attitudes during the 1990s."},{"title":"International Social Survey Programme: Role of Government III, 1996","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/issp/modules/issp-modules-by-topic/role-of-government","justification":"A cross-national survey examining attitudes toward government responsibilities, public spending, welfare provision, economic redistribution, and the relationship between citizens and the state. Its 1996 British observations are particularly relevant for analysing political values, support for government intervention, economic inequality, and public perceptions of government institutions during the 1990s."},{"title":"International Social Survey Programme: Social Inequality II, 1992","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/issp/modules/issp-modules-by-topic/social-inequality","justification":"A comparative survey investigating perceptions of social inequality, economic fairness, social mobility, class differences, and income distribution. The 1992 British observations are valuable for analysing social stratification, attitudes toward redistribution, perceptions of economic opportunity, and public beliefs about the causes of inequality during the early 1990s."},{"title":"International Social Survey Programme: National Identity I, 1995","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/issp/modules/issp-modules-by-topic/national-identity","justification":"A comparative survey module investigating national identity, patriotism, national belonging, attitudes toward immigrants, and perceptions of national institutions. The 1995 British data provide insight into social identity, political values, cultural attitudes, and social divisions. It is particularly useful for exploring relationships between national identification, social background, and political attitudes in the United Kingdom."},{"title":"International Social Survey Programme: Work Orientations II, 1997","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/issp/modules/issp-modules-by-topic/work-orientations","justification":"A comparative survey examining employment-related values, job satisfaction, working conditions, employment preferences, and attitudes toward work. The 1997 British observations are relevant for investigating economic behaviour, social stratification, labour-market experiences, and the relationship between employment circumstances and social attitudes during the late 1990s."},{"title":"1991 Census Microdata Collections, UK Data Service","url_or_doi":"https://ukdataservice.ac.uk/learning-hub/census/resources/get-census-microdata/","justification":"An official UK Data Service resource providing access information for individual and household samples from the 1991 Census, including separate datasets for Great Britain and Northern Ireland. These datasets support research on social stratification, demographic composition, marriage, family structure, employment, occupational inequalities, and economic characteristics. They are particularly useful for establishing nationally representative socioeconomic conditions at the beginning of the 1990s."}]}
